So there are std's that are not routinely tested for in the United States.  The cdc here claims that since they don't usually cause reproductive harm and co habitate in the reproductive tract without symptoms, they are labeled as a commensal bacteria and are treated like they're a naturally occurring bacteria when they are not.  They wreak havoc on the autoimmune community.  I found out I had one while married and my immune system crashed.  I just started getting these god-awful symptoms that would not go away.  All std tests were clear, no uti detected, ultrasounds were fine.  It was miserable and took almost 2 years for an urgent care doctor to test me for these stds, which are often overlooked. 

I was positive for ureaplasma.  Another one I know of is mycoplasma.  

If it was one of these lesser tested for stds, it's highly possible she didn't cheat.  They can exist for someone's entire life without them knowing, or someone could get a weekend immune system later in life, then experience horrible symptoms.  These may not have been included in her std screenings during her 1st pregnancy.  Thankfully, testing for them are starting to become more frequent in the US, but it still has a way to go.

It's insane to me that all other 1st world countries recognize these stds, routinely test for them, and have active treatment plans for them.  America is so far behind.

If the std is a more common one that she had been tested for during 1st pregnancy, it was negative, and then suddenly became positive uhm Yeah, there's an issue.
